Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

picreg 0.2.0

Breaking changes

  • The relax argument of pic() has been removed. To debias the coefficients, refit on fit$selected with the estimator of your choice (e.g. lm() or glm()).

  • For Cox fits, predict(type = "response") now returns the relative risk exp(eta), as in glmnet, instead of the linear predictor, and coef() no longer has an (Intercept) row.

  • For SCAD and MCP, the solver now follows Section 3.3 of the paper: the l1 path runs down to the target lambda, and the SCAD / MCP stage starts from that l1 solution (it previously started from the l1 solution at the penultimate path value). Selected supports may differ slightly from previous versions.

  • The default number of Monte Carlo draws is now 2000 everywhere, as in the paper: lambda_pdb(), phase_transition() and pdb_asymptotic() used

  • With intercept = FALSE and standardize = TRUE, the (Intercept) row of coef() now absorbs the centering of the columns on the original scale, so that coef() reproduces predict(). It is zero when X is centered.

  • fit$beta is now a plain numeric vector (it was a one-column matrix).

New features

  • pic() accepts a pic.lambda_pdb object as lambda, typically fit$lambda_pdb, to reuse a calibration across penalties while keeping it on the new fit for pdb_summary() and plot(). Its family and design dimensions are checked.

  • New lambda_seed argument of pic() and seed argument of lambda_pdb() for a reproducible PDB calibration. Only the calibration is seeded: the global random stream is restored afterwards. Default NULL.

  • Binomial responses may be logical (TRUE mapped to 1) or a two-level factor (second level mapped to 1). assess() maps new responses with the training levels.

  • Fits store the matched call, the total number of FISTA iterations n_iter and a converged flag, and pic() warns when the final FISTA step reaches maxit.

  • lambda_pdb() results also store seed, family, n and p.

  • phase_transition():

    • failed fits are excluded from the averages, counted in a new n_failed column of results and reported in a single warning (they were silently counted as failed recoveries);
    • with parallel = TRUE, the caller’s future plan is restored on exit (it was reset to sequential), and workers defaults to future::availableCores(omit = 1), which honors the core limits set by CRAN or a scheduler.

Bug fixes

  • feature_effects_on_survival() failed on Cox fits with standardize = FALSE.

  • A constant column of X triggered a spurious “does not appear standardized” warning. Constant columns are also detected robustly to rounding.

  • Arguments of pic() and lambda_pdb() are validated with explicit messages. Previously, e.g., lambda = c(0.1, 0.2) gave a cryptic error, lambda = -1 produced NaNs and lambda_alpha = 0 an infinite lambda.

  • predict() reports a mismatch between the number of columns of newx and of the training X.

  • print() of a phase_transition() result listed no curve, and print() of a family descriptor missed its final newline.

  • Gumbel family:

    • the null intercept and scale, used for the warm start, lambda_max and the "mc_exact" calibration, are now the joint location-scale maximum-likelihood estimates (previously a moment-based intercept followed by a conditional scale estimate);
    • the profiled scale is solved by a bracketed, safeguarded Newton method without clipping the exponentials, and the loss and gradient share a single solve;
    • fitting is numerically stable under large shifts of the response, and a constant response raises an explicit error;
    • assess() reports the deviance with the scale profiled at its maximum-likelihood estimate instead of a moment estimate.

Performance

  • The Monte Carlo PDB calibration processes the draws in blocks, which bounds its memory (it allocated two n x n_simu matrices, about 640 MB for n = 20000) without changing the result for a given seed. The Cox permutation calibration stores the simulated events as bytes.

  • concordance_index() is computed in C++ in O(n log n) time and O(n) memory instead of O(n^2) matrices, and cox_partial_log_likelihood() no longer loops over the unique times.

  • The Cox solver evaluates the loss and its gradient in a single pass over the risk sets and no longer records unused per-iteration diagnostics.

  • The per-column value grids used by feature_effects_on_survival() are only computed for Cox fits (they were computed and discarded for every family, which dominated preprocessing for wide designs). feature_effects_on_survival() predicts all values in one call.

Dependencies

  • future and future.apply move from Imports to Suggests: they are only needed for phase_transition(parallel = TRUE). parallel is no longer used.

Documentation

  • Fixed the documentation of lambda_pdb() (probability of selecting a variable under the null, tightness of the Bonferroni bound), of the selected and beta components of a fit, and of the value returned by phase_transition(), plus several typos in the vignette (formulas of the Gaussian and exponential objectives, PBD, section references).

  • The vignette comparison with glmnet uses random signs for the non-zero coefficients, as stated in the text.

picreg 0.1.4

CRAN release: 2026-07-20

New features

  • predict() for Cox fits now accepts type = "survival", which returns subject-specific survival curves (a list with time and survival components). This replaces the standalone predict_survival_function(), which has been removed.

Breaking changes

  • predict_survival_function() has been removed. Use predict(object, newx, type = "survival") instead.

picreg 0.1.3

CRAN release: 2026-06-04

Bug fixes

  • Resolved a C++ One Definition Rule (ODR) violation reported under link-time optimization (LTO): the file-local helper structs in fista.cpp and fista_cox.cpp now have internal linkage (anonymous namespaces).

Minor improvements

  • coef() now returns a one-column sparse matrix instead of a two-column data frame. Zero coefficients are printed as ., which keeps the display compact in high dimensions.

  • Added a summary() method for pic fits.

  • intercept = FALSE is now permitted for every family. Previously it raised an error for non-Cox families when standardize = TRUE. When intercept = FALSE, the data are assumed to be centered.

  • Standardized the input-validation error messages (consistent back-quoting of argument names and call. = FALSE).
